hardware: All workers used one physical GPU. The two source checkouts and precisions had separate compiler, Triton and CUDA caches.
equivalent_single_checkout_cli: python scripts/bench_cores.py --only schnet --systems acceptance --compile-reference --model-tree CHECKOUT --device cuda --dtype PRECISION --threads 2 --reps 9 --out RESULTS.json
compilation_mode: --compile-reference (Inductor fullgraph, same functional force and table gather on both checkouts)
measurement: Paired workers call the pinned driver's _batch, compile_reference_model and core_harness.forward. Controlled weights, gradient checks and opposite-order repetitions are applied by the paired runner.

controls.gpu_state_units: NVIDIA performance state, SM MHz, memory MHz, temperature in Celsius, sampled after the timed observations when available. The first FP32 pair could not sample clocks.
controls.weights: Every worker strictly reloads the same seed-0 frozen default SchNet state, translated with convert_state_dict on the candidate. The full parameter multiset hash is checked after casting to the measured dtype.
controls.extra_rounds: A change above +3% in either initial pair triggers rounds three and four for that precision.
controls.pairing: Per round, compare the medians of nine observations in separate new processes. The primary comparison uses the ratio of pooled sample medians, overall and within each run order. The geometric mean of per-round median ratios is also reported as an order-balanced check.
controls.numeric: Each checkout's compiled outputs are compared to its own eager outputs. Parameter gradients of sum(E**2) + sum(Fa**2) are checked individually by relative L2 or maximum absolute error.
controls.checkpoint_scale_diagnostic: These runs use the pre-refactor devel checkout. For reference we also report E/F against the main-compatibility scales: FP64 max absolute error <= 1e-10 and FP32 max absolute error / max(1, max absolute baseline) <= 1e-6.
